- Please do NOT operate any electrical switches (lights, extractor, doorbell), do not use the cooker or any naked flame, do not smoke.
- Open all windows and doors if safe to do so; turn off the gas at the meter (emergency control valve) only if it is safe and easy to reach.
- Because the smell is strong and your wife has a headache: everyone (and any pets) should leave the property now and wait outside.
- Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 straight away (free, 24/7) - they will attend and make the supply safe. Use a mobile phone outside the property.
- Headache can be a sign of gas or carbon monoxide exposure: if anyone feels dizzy, sick, short of breath or the headache worsens, call 999; otherwise contact NHS 111 for advice.
- Ask: have you called 0800 111 999 yet? Is everyone out of the property? Is anyone else in the home (children, elderly, pregnant, pets)?
- Reassure: you will not be charged for this; gas safety is the landlord's legal responsibility. Our property manager is handling it now and we will arrange a Gas Safe registered engineer for the follow-up repair. Please tell us the gas emergency reference and what the engineer says when they attend.

input.body:
Address: 9 Birch Close, Croydon CR0 7EX
Ref: TKT-8A472B

Hi Marcus,

This is to let you know about an emergency at your property today (Fri 10 Oct). At 08:15 the tenant reported: "There's a really strong smell of gas in the kitchen this morning, near the cooker. My wife's got a headache."

What we have done: we have told the tenants to leave the property, not to use any switches or flames, and to call the National Gas Emergency Service (0800 111 999), who will make the supply safe. We are arranging a Gas Safe registered engineer to find and repair the fault, and our property manager is handling the case.

Please note:
- Fixing a suspected gas leak is an emergency and a legal repair duty for the landlord (s.11 Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 and the Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998). Under our policy, emergency make-safe work goes ahead without waiting for approval and we tell you the same day. We will send you an estimate before any further repair work goes ahead that costs more than your £150 limit.
- The gas safety certificate for the property ran out on 30 Sep 2026. A yearly gas safety check is a legal requirement for let properties. We recommend the engineer renews the certificate while they are there, and our property manager will contact you about this.

We know you have said before that you do not want to be billed for gas work. We cannot leave a gas safety issue unrepaired, and our property manager will be in touch. Please reply by email with any questions.

Kind regards,
Resolve AI - Maintenance Operations
